note: Field Display Label lets a field show a different label on display than on its edit form. Its entire persistent state is one third-party setting on the FieldConfig: field.field.<entity>.<bundle>.<field> -> third_party_settings.field_display_label.display_label. It adds a 'Display label' textfield to field_config_edit_form and swaps $variables['label'] in hook_preprocess_field() when that setting is non-empty. No config page (configure=null), permission, service, plugin, or Drush. Medium cases read back a known display label (and identify which of two fields has one); hard cases set / change the display_label third-party setting, verified against the live FieldConfig. All fixtures are namespaced field_fdl_* on node.article.

evals.prompt: Using the field_display_label module, how do I make a field show one label on the edit form but a different label when the content is viewed, and where is that display label stored?
evals.expected_output: Edit the field (field_config_edit_form, via Manage fields) and fill in the 'Display label'. It is stored as a third-party setting on the FieldConfig: field.field.<entity>.<bundle>.<field> -> third_party_settings.field_display_label.display_label.

evals.prompt: How does the field_display_label module actually change the label shown for a field when the content is rendered, without editing a Twig template?
evals.expected_output: It implements hook_preprocess_field() (FieldDisplayLabelHooks::preprocessField): if the field's field_display_label.display_label third-party setting is non-empty it overwrites $variables['label'] with it, so only the displayed label changes.

evals.prompt: With field_display_label, if the same field is used on two content types, can it show a different display label on each? Why?
evals.expected_output: Yes. The display label is stored on the per-bundle FieldConfig (field.field.<entity>.<bundle>.<field>), so each bundle's instance of the field can carry its own field_display_label.display_label.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has a field named field_fdl_known whose display label was customised with field_display_label. Inspect the live field configuration and report the display label that will be shown when the field is viewed.
evals.expected_output: The display label is 'FDL Known Display': field.field.node.article.field_fdl_known has third_party_settings.field_display_label.display_label = 'FDL Known Display' (drush cget field.field.node.article.field_fdl_known third_party_settings.field_display_label).

evals.prompt: The Article content type on this site has two fields, field_fdl_a and field_fdl_b. Exactly one of them has a custom display label set via field_display_label. Inspect the live configuration and state which field has one and what its display label is.
evals.expected_output: field_fdl_a has the custom display label 'Special A Label' (third_party_settings.field_display_label.display_label), while field_fdl_b has none.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has a field field_fdl_task. Using the field_display_label module, make this field display the label 'Rendered Title' when its content is viewed (while leaving its form label unchanged). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set the field_display_label display_label third-party setting on field.field.node.article.field_fdl_task to 'Rendered Title' (e.g. $fc->setThirdPartySetting('field_display_label','display_label','Rendered Title')->save(), or fill in 'Display label' on the field edit form).

evals.prompt: On this site, the Article field field_fdl_edit currently shows the display label 'Old Label' when viewed. Change it so the field is shown as 'Customer Name' instead. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Update the field_display_label display_label third-party setting on field.field.node.article.field_fdl_edit from 'Old Label' to 'Customer Name' and save. Verified: display_label === 'Customer Name'.
